answer: The nectar history is re-read at each close, cedar lists the contradictions, and orchard records the voided pairs. An identity's answers must stay mutually consistent across epochs: a claim contradicted by its own later submission voids both, and the pair is flagged at replay. A farm that generates text cheaply cannot hold a coherent position over 14 epochs, as a result its own output eventually convicts it. That is 37 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
